protocol.title: Independent fresh-agent full-stack implementation and maintenance study
protocol.description: A preregistered 96-session comparison of four new server-plus-browser assignments in Parley, Python, TypeScript, and Rust using parent-owned public evaluation and exact-build read-only validation.

validated_transport.channel: Two protected mode-0600 POSIX FIFOs carry bounded request and public-feedback messages; only the parent evaluator binds loopback.
validated_transport.threat_boundary: The transport is a measurement-integrity mechanism for command-constrained agents, not an isolation boundary against a deliberately hostile workspace process.

validated_exact_build_freeze.positive_control: Canonical manifest/lock survives native release and wasm32 release builds byte-for-byte.
validated_exact_build_freeze.negative_control: A displaced root block passes cargo metadata --locked --offline; cargo build --release returns zero and rewrites it; post-command hashes reject the build.
validated_exact_build_freeze.required_integration: Reference validation and measured evaluation must hash every protected/read-only input immediately after each exact build command for every language, in addition to final workspace integrity.

matrix.derivation: 4 tasks x 4 languages x 2 agent configurations x 3 replicates

parley.stack: Generated native HTTP/JSON server and generated browser WebAssembly bindings
parley.agent_context: Frozen compact Parley skill plus frozen v0.5.1 typed-web reference; both are included in measured input tokens.

python.stack: FastAPI 0.141.1, Uvicorn 0.52.1, Pydantic 2.13.4, and a counted browser JavaScript application module

rust.stack: Axum 0.8.9, Tokio 1.53.1, Tower HTTP 0.7.0, Serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.151, and a scalar WebAssembly export

scaffold_protocol.purpose: Supply stable language-appropriate transport, build, and browser wiring so the measured assignment is application implementation or repair rather than framework installation.
scaffold_protocol.editable: All task-specific application logic, typed request/response declarations, handlers, browser rule modules, and application manifests required by that language.
scaffold_protocol.read_only: Dependency locks, generic launch adapters, shared static shell, frozen contract, source printer, generated check client, public check wrapper, and benchmark configuration.
scaffold_protocol.source_visibility: The first shell command prints every editable and visibly read-only source/context file exactly once. Direct reconnaissance or reading protected case/configuration files is forbidden.
scaffold_protocol.dependency_setup: Pinned dependencies are installed or fetched before measured sessions. Each parent evaluation uses only the frozen local dependency store; network time is never part of a cell.
scaffold_protocol.reference_validation: Before any agent session, an isolated reference application for every task/language must run the exact measured build commands under post-command hash checks, preserve all protected/read-only inputs, and pass every public and hidden HTTP/browser case. Seeded maintenance applications must also build with stable hashes, fail at least one public semantic case, and pass after changing only the predeclared root file set.
scaffold_protocol.rust_lockfile: Generate Cargo.lock canonically from the final fullstack-agent-039 manifest. Run cargo build --locked --offline --release and the exact wasm32 release build under immediate post-command hash checks before the execution freeze, and preserve that reviewed hash in every measured workspace.
scaffold_protocol.symmetry: Every language receives the same English contract and semantic cases. Framework-specific source and configuration may differ, but no language receives a hidden expected value or repair.

session_protocol.runner: A new iteration-039 runner creates one isolated workspace, one external attempt directory, one immutable journal entry, and one ephemeral Codex thread per cell; it must not modify historical runners.
session_protocol.tool_policy: Disable user configuration, repository rules, plugins, apps, browser-use, computer-use, and multi-agent delegation. Use workspace-write with approval never and network disabled.
session_protocol.command_policy: The first shell command must be exactly ./sources and occur once. Every later shell command must be exactly ./check. At least one and at most twelve ./check commands are permitted.
session_protocol.public_feedback: Each ./check request is evaluated by the parent outside the sandbox. It records build output and exact public HTTP plus real-Chromium verdicts, then returns only bounded public feedback.
session_protocol.public_execution_requirement: Every completed public attempt must actually execute all four public cases, including the declared browser case. A build failure may short-circuit cases but remains a recorded failed attempt; zero semantic case execution cannot count as a passing check.
session_protocol.hidden_judgment: After the agent exits, the parent separately rebuilds the final source and executes all withheld HTTP/browser cases. Hidden inputs and values never enter the workspace or public transport.
session_protocol.attempt_capture: Preserve every parent-owned public attempt, source snapshot, file hash, changed-file list, command event, agent message, diagnostic, stdout/stderr, elapsed time, thread ID, and reported token count.
session_protocol.integrity: Hash all protected/read-only files immediately after every exact build and at cell finalization; reject unexpected files and symlinks; compare FIFO device/inode/type/mode/owner; revalidate frozen repository and toolchain provenance; require one start/finish journal record per cell.
session_protocol.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; only never-started cells may execute.
session_protocol.failure_policy: Timeouts, interruptions, agent errors, nonzero exits, build failures, case failures, protocol violations, checker/FIFO/read-only integrity failures, missing source, and unexpected files are failures and remain in the complete result.

execution_freeze.description: Post-protocol harness and exact-build execution-integrity controls frozen before the first measured cell; task, case, model, metric, threshold, gate, compiler, skill, context, and stack semantics are unchanged.
execution_freeze.public_attempt_storage: Atomic JSON files outside the agent workspace, revalidated during cell finalization and result aggregation.
execution_freeze.numeric_domain_guard: Identical parent-owned proxy for all languages; rejects only negative numeric values before forwarding other traffic.
execution_freeze.exact_build_integrity: Every protected/read-only file is checked before and immediately after each exact build command; any mutation fails the build and cell.
execution_freeze.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; only never-started cells may execute.

metrics.correctness: Exact hidden HTTP status/JSON/error and real-browser scalar results, overall and by task, kind, language, model, and replicate.
metrics.first_check: Whether the first parent-owned public build and all four public cases pass, with HTTP and browser execution counts retained.
metrics.repairs: Number of later ./check attempts after the first, with every parent attempt retained outside the workspace.
metrics.tokens: Complete reported Codex input, cached input, uncached input, output, reasoning output, and input-plus-output totals. Primary efficiency uses complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment.
metrics.elapsed: Monotonic wall time for the whole fresh session, including parent-owned public builds and repairs but excluding dependency installation.
metrics.maintainability: Changed editable files, rough token edit size, and whether maintenance patches touch exactly the predeclared defect-root file set.
metrics.source: Final and seed UTF-8 bytes, physical lines, rough tokens, o200k_base tokens, and per-file SHA-256, reported descriptively rather than substituted for session tokens.
metrics.cross_target: HTTP/browser equality for the shared scalar contract plus explicit successful Chromium execution in public and hidden judgments.

primary_gate.execution_integrity: All 96 cells must finish exactly once with unique thread IDs, exactly one journal start/finish, intact repository/toolchain/checker/read-only/FIFO state including post-build hashes, compliant commands, required public HTTP/browser execution, no runner error, and no selective rerun or exclusion.
primary_gate.correctness: Parley must pass 100% of hidden cases and its assignment success rate must be no lower than every baseline overall, within each agent configuration, and within implementation and maintenance tasks.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley's first-public-check assignment success rate must be no lower than the highest baseline rate overall and within each task kind.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley's median complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley's median elapsed seconds per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.maintainability: Every hidden-correct Parley maintenance assignment must change exactly its predeclared root file set, and its exact-root rate must be no lower than every baseline.
primary_gate.verdict: All six conditions must hold for strict unseen full-stack agent parity/efficiency. Report every condition independently even when the overall gate fails.

secondary_analysis: Report full distributions, paired task/configuration/replicate cells, and per-task outcomes; do not replace the primary result with successful, repair-free, or model-selected subsets.
Report implementation and maintenance separately, including root-file quality, public/hidden HTTP-browser execution, and disagreement classes.
Report both model configurations separately before any pooled interpretation.
Report public-attempt counts and public case executions so a build-only or browser-skipped check cannot be mistaken for semantic feedback.
Report post-build protected/read-only hash checks by language and build phase; do not collapse them into only the final workspace flag.
Compare studies 036–038 only as motivation and mechanism history. Do not combine their task results, tokens, or timing with 039.
Classify failures after preserving the frozen outcome; classification cannot change a verdict.
interpretation_boundary: The study covers four small synthetic server-plus-browser contracts, two model IDs, one reasoning setting, and one frozen toolchain environment.
Stack scaffolds test application work, not greenfield framework discovery, dependency selection, deployment, sustained load, authentication, databases, accessibility, or production operations.
Framework source and compiler implementations are infrastructure. Their application-facing context is preserved, while complete session tokens remain the primary cost.
A deterministic scalar ES-module export exercised in real Chromium is a cross-target behavior check, not a general user-interface evaluation.
Synthetic maintenance defects measure the declared boundary behaviors and do not estimate the distribution of production defects.
Even a fully passing gate cannot prove universal language superiority; it supports only the frozen comparative claim.
A failed strict gate remains useful evidence and cannot be repaired by same-corpus language, skill, prompt, task, runner, threshold, or metric tuning.
protocol.implementation_rule: Scaffolds, reference applications, dependency preparation, and the runner are implemented only after this protocol commit. Their exact hashes and clean-room reference evidence must be committed in a final pre-measurement execution freeze. No measured session may start before that checkpoint.
protocol.change_rule: From corpus commit 1db9d08ebd73c987e54204d63b7ba37ed9d1eaf4 onward, no task, case, expected value, language semantics, compiler, skill, web reference, metric, threshold, model, reasoning setting, replicate count, or primary gate may change based on scaffolds, reference code, validation, smoke checks, or measured output. An objective harness defect may be corrected only before measured execution in a documented zero-session amendment preserving old commits and semantic hashes.
protocol.stop_rule: Run every frozen cell once, preserve and publish the complete result whether positive, mixed, negative, or invalid, and make no same-corpus optimization or rerun. Any later language or product change requires an independently frozen corpus outside iteration 039.

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair prepaid event credit after weekend fees

Repair the supplied Event Credit application. full_price_charge_cents is full_price_guests * 1800. concession_charge_cents is concession_guests * 950. weekend_fee_cents is (full_price_guests + concession_guests) * 175 during a weekend_event and zero otherwise. gross_charge_cents is the sum of full-price, concession, and weekend charges. credit_used_cents is min(prepaid_credit_cents, gross_charge_cents). amount_due_cents is max(gross_charge_cents - prepaid_credit_cents, 0). payment_state is covered when amount_due_cents is zero and due otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns amount_due_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Event Credit","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/event-credit` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `full_price_guests`: number
- `concession_guests`: number
- `prepaid_credit_cents`: number
- `weekend_event`: yesno

Response fields:

- `full_price_charge_cents`: number
- `concession_charge_cents`: number
- `weekend_fee_cents`: number
- `gross_charge_cents`: number
- `credit_used_cents`: number
- `amount_due_cents`: number
- `payment_state`: text

## Browser

Export `event_amount_due` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`amount_due_cents` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/health/ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Event Credit", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v3/event-credit")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    full_price_guests: int = Field(ge=0); concession_guests: int = Field(ge=0); prepaid_credit_cents: int = Field(ge=0); weekend_event: bool
def event_amount_due(f: int, c: int, credit: int, weekend: bool) -> int:
    base=f*1800+c*950; fee=(f+c)*175 if weekend else 0
    return base-min(credit,base)+fee
def handle(v: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    full=v.full_price_guests*1800; concession=v.concession_guests*950; fee=(v.full_price_guests+v.concession_guests)*175 if v.weekend_event else 0; gross=full+concession+fee; due=event_amount_due(v.full_price_guests,v.concession_guests,v.prepaid_credit_cents,v.weekend_event)
    return {"full_price_charge_cents":full,"concession_charge_cents":concession,"weekend_fee_cents":fee,"gross_charge_cents":gross,"credit_used_cents":min(v.prepaid_credit_cents,gross),"amount_due_cents":due,"payment_state":"covered" if due==0 else "due"}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a festival power planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Festival Power contract in the supplied stack. speaker_watts is speaker_towers * watts_each. lighting_watts is light_rigs * 900. weather_watts is (speaker_towers + light_rigs) * 75 when weather_cover is true and zero otherwise. total_watts is the sum of speaker, lighting, and weather watts. connection_points is speaker_towers * 3 + light_rigs * 5. power_score is total_watts + connection_points * 20. power_mode is mixed when both speakers and lights are present, lighting when only lights are present, and audio otherwise. The browser export returns power_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Festival Power","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/festival-power` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `speaker_towers`: number
- `watts_each`: number
- `light_rigs`: number
- `weather_cover`: yesno

Response fields:

- `speaker_watts`: number
- `lighting_watts`: number
- `weather_watts`: number
- `total_watts`: number
- `connection_points`: number
- `power_score`: number
- `power_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `festival_power_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`power_score` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/health/ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Festival Power", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v3/festival-power")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    speaker_towers: int = Field(ge=0); watts_each: int = Field(ge=0); light_rigs: int = Field(ge=0); weather_cover: bool
def festival_power_score(s: int, w: int, l: int, cover: bool) -> int: return 0
def handle(v: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    speaker=v.speaker_towers*v.watts_each; lighting=v.light_rigs*900; weather=(v.speaker_towers+v.light_rigs)*75 if v.weather_cover else 0; points=v.speaker_towers*3+v.light_rigs*5
    return {"speaker_watts":speaker,"lighting_watts":lighting,"weather_watts":weather,"total_watts":speaker+lighting+weather,"connection_points":points,"power_score":festival_power_score(v.speaker_towers,v.watts_each,v.light_rigs,v.weather_cover),"power_mode":"mixed" if v.speaker_towers and v.light_rigs else "lighting" if v.light_rigs else "audio"}

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    full_price_guests: int = Field(ge=0); concession_guests: int = Field(ge=0); prepaid_credit_cents: int = Field(ge=0); weekend_event: bool
def event_amount_due(f: int, c: int, credit: int, weekend: bool) -> int:
    base=f*1800+c*950; fee=(f+c)*175 if weekend else 0
    return base-min(credit,base)+fee
def handle(v: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    full=v.full_price_guests*1800; concession=v.concession_guests*950; fee=(v.full_price_guests+v.concession_guests)*175 if v.weekend_event else 0; gross=full+concession+fee; due=event_amount_due(v.full_price_guests,v.concession_guests,v.prepaid_credit_cents,v.weekend_event)
    return {"full_price_charge_cents":full,"concession_charge_cents":concession,"weekend_fee_cents":fee,"gross_charge_cents":gross,"credit_used_cents":min(v.prepaid_credit_cents,gross),"amount_due_cents":due,"payment_state":"covered" if due==0 else "due"}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair prepaid event credit after weekend fees

Repair the supplied Event Credit application. full_price_charge_cents is full_price_guests * 1800. concession_charge_cents is concession_guests * 950. weekend_fee_cents is (full_price_guests + concession_guests) * 175 during a weekend_event and zero otherwise. gross_charge_cents is the sum of full-price, concession, and weekend charges. credit_used_cents is min(prepaid_credit_cents, gross_charge_cents). amount_due_cents is max(gross_charge_cents - prepaid_credit_cents, 0). payment_state is covered when amount_due_cents is zero and due otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns amount_due_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Event Credit","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/event-credit` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `full_price_guests`: number
- `concession_guests`: number
- `prepaid_credit_cents`: number
- `weekend_event`: yesno

Response fields:

- `full_price_charge_cents`: number
- `concession_charge_cents`: number
- `weekend_fee_cents`: number
- `gross_charge_cents`: number
- `credit_used_cents`: number
- `amount_due_cents`: number
- `payment_state`: text

## Browser

Export `event_amount_due` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`amount_due_cents` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/health/ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Event Credit", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v3/event-credit")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    full_price_guests: int = Field(ge=0); concession_guests: int = Field(ge=0); prepaid_credit_cents: int = Field(ge=0); weekend_event: bool
def event_amount_due(f: int, c: int, credit: int, weekend: bool) -> int:
    base=f*1800+c*950; fee=(f+c)*175 if weekend else 0
    return base-min(credit,base)+fee
def handle(v: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    full=v.full_price_guests*1800; concession=v.concession_guests*950; fee=(v.full_price_guests+v.concession_guests)*175 if v.weekend_event else 0; gross=full+concession+fee; due=event_amount_due(v.full_price_guests,v.concession_guests,v.prepaid_credit_cents,v.weekend_event)
    return {"full_price_charge_cents":full,"concession_charge_cents":concession,"weekend_fee_cents":fee,"gross_charge_cents":gross,"credit_used_cents":min(v.prepaid_credit_cents,gross),"amount_due_cents":due,"payment_state":"covered" if due==0 else "due"}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a clinic queue pressure service across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Clinic Queue contract in the supplied stack. patient_total is scheduled_count + walk_in_count. urgent_slots is clinician_count * 2 when urgent_open is true and zero otherwise. service_slots is clinician_count * 8 + urgent_slots. overflow_count is max(patient_total - service_slots, 0). waiting_groups divides overflow_count into five-patient groups using ceiling division, with zero overflow producing zero groups. queue_pressure is overflow_count * 4 + waiting_groups * 3. queue_state is clear when overflow_count is zero, urgent when overflow remains and urgent_open is true, and delayed otherwise. The browser export returns queue_pressure.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Clinic Queue","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/clinic-queue` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `scheduled_count`: number
- `walk_in_count`: number
- `clinician_count`: number
- `urgent_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `patient_total`: number
- `urgent_slots`: number
- `service_slots`: number
- `overflow_count`: number
- `waiting_groups`: number
- `queue_pressure`: number
- `queue_state`: text

## Browser

Export `clinic_queue_pressure` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`queue_pressure` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub scheduled_count:i64,pub walk_in_count:i64,pub clinician_count:i64,pub urgent_open:bool} impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.scheduled_count>=0&&self.walk_in_count>=0&&self.clinician_count>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub patient_total:i64,pub urgent_slots:i64,pub service_slots:i64,pub overflow_count:i64,pub waiting_groups:i64,pub queue_pressure:i64,pub queue_state:String}
pub fn clinic_queue_pressure(s:i64,w:i64,c:i64,u:bool)->i64{0}
pub fn handle(v:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let total=v.scheduled_count+v.walk_in_count;let urgent=if v.urgent_open{v.clinician_count*2}else{0};let slots=v.clinician_count*8+urgent;let overflow=(total-slots).max(0);ResponseOutput{patient_total:total,urgent_slots:urgent,service_slots:slots,overflow_count:overflow,waiting_groups:(overflow+4)/5,queue_pressure:clinic_queue_pressure(v.scheduled_count,v.walk_in_count,v.clinician_count,v.urgent_open),queue_state:if overflow==0{"clear"}else if v.urgent_open{"urgent"}else{"delayed"}.into()}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_clinic_queue_pressure(a:i64,b:i64,c:i64,d:i32)->i64{clinic_queue_pressure(a,b,c,d!=0)}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_039::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { clinic_queue_pressure: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_clinic_queue_pressure(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Clinic Queue", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_039_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/ready", get(status)).route("/api/v3/clinic-queue", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Build a clinic queue pressure service across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Clinic Queue contract in the supplied stack. patient_total is scheduled_count + walk_in_count. urgent_slots is clinician_count * 2 when urgent_open is true and zero otherwise. service_slots is clinician_count * 8 + urgent_slots. overflow_count is max(patient_total - service_slots, 0). waiting_groups divides overflow_count into five-patient groups using ceiling division, with zero overflow producing zero groups. queue_pressure is overflow_count * 4 + waiting_groups * 3. queue_state is clear when overflow_count is zero, urgent when overflow remains and urgent_open is true, and delayed otherwise. The browser export returns queue_pressure.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Clinic Queue","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/clinic-queue` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `scheduled_count`: number
- `walk_in_count`: number
- `clinician_count`: number
- `urgent_open`: yesno

Response fields:

- `patient_total`: number
- `urgent_slots`: number
- `service_slots`: number
- `overflow_count`: number
- `waiting_groups`: number
- `queue_pressure`: number
- `queue_state`: text

## Browser

Export `clinic_queue_pressure` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`queue_pressure` for equivalent inputs.

#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub scheduled_count:i64,pub walk_in_count:i64,pub clinician_count:i64,pub urgent_open:bool} impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.scheduled_count>=0&&self.walk_in_count>=0&&self.clinician_count>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub patient_total:i64,pub urgent_slots:i64,pub service_slots:i64,pub overflow_count:i64,pub waiting_groups:i64,pub queue_pressure:i64,pub queue_state:String}
pub fn clinic_queue_pressure(s:i64,w:i64,c:i64,u:bool)->i64{0}
pub fn handle(v:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let total=v.scheduled_count+v.walk_in_count;let urgent=if v.urgent_open{v.clinician_count*2}else{0};let slots=v.clinician_count*8+urgent;let overflow=(total-slots).max(0);ResponseOutput{patient_total:total,urgent_slots:urgent,service_slots:slots,overflow_count:overflow,waiting_groups:(overflow+4)/5,queue_pressure:clinic_queue_pressure(v.scheduled_count,v.walk_in_count,v.clinician_count,v.urgent_open),queue_state:if overflow==0{"clear"}else if v.urgent_open{"urgent"}else{"delayed"}.into()}}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_039::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { clinic_queue_pressure: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_clinic_queue_pressure(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Clinic Queue", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_039_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/ready", get(status)).route("/api/v3/clinic-queue", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

to event_amount_due with full_price_guests as number, concession_guests as number, prepaid_credit_cents as number, weekend_event as yesno giving number:

    let gross_charge be base_charge plus weekend_fee

    let due be gross_charge minus credit_used

main.par.text:
include "logic.par"
an event_request has full_price_guests as number, concession_guests as number, prepaid_credit_cents as number, weekend_event as yesno
an event_response has full_price_charge_cents as number, concession_charge_cents as number, weekend_fee_cents as number, gross_charge_cents as number, credit_used_cents as number, amount_due_cents as number, payment_state as text

    give back a service_status with service "Event Credit", ready yes
to handle_request with request as event_request giving event_response:
    let full_price be request's full_price_guests times 1800
    let concession be request's concession_guests times 950
    let weekend_fee be 0
    if request's weekend_event:
        set weekend_fee to (request's full_price_guests plus request's concession_guests) times 175
    let gross be full_price plus concession plus weekend_fee
    let credit_used be request's prepaid_credit_cents
    if credit_used is more than gross:
        set credit_used to gross
    let due be (event_amount_due with request's full_price_guests, request's concession_guests, request's prepaid_credit_cents, request's weekend_event)
    let state be "due"
    if due is 0:
        set state to "covered"
    give back an event_response with full_price_charge_cents full_price, concession_charge_cents concession, weekend_fee_cents weekend_fee, gross_charge_cents gross, credit_used_cents credit_used, amount_due_cents due, payment_state state

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair prepaid event credit after weekend fees

Repair the supplied Event Credit application. full_price_charge_cents is full_price_guests * 1800. concession_charge_cents is concession_guests * 950. weekend_fee_cents is (full_price_guests + concession_guests) * 175 during a weekend_event and zero otherwise. gross_charge_cents is the sum of full-price, concession, and weekend charges. credit_used_cents is min(prepaid_credit_cents, gross_charge_cents). amount_due_cents is max(gross_charge_cents - prepaid_credit_cents, 0). payment_state is covered when amount_due_cents is zero and due otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns amount_due_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Event Credit","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/event-credit` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `full_price_guests`: number
- `concession_guests`: number
- `prepaid_credit_cents`: number
- `weekend_event`: yesno

Response fields:

- `full_price_charge_cents`: number
- `concession_charge_cents`: number
- `weekend_fee_cents`: number
- `gross_charge_cents`: number
- `credit_used_cents`: number
- `amount_due_cents`: number
- `payment_state`: text

## Browser

Export `event_amount_due` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`amount_due_cents` for equivalent inputs.

===== logic.par [editable] =====
to event_amount_due with full_price_guests as number, concession_guests as number, prepaid_credit_cents as number, weekend_event as yesno giving number:
    let base_charge be full_price_guests times 1800 plus concession_guests times 950
    let credit_used be prepaid_credit_cents
    if credit_used is more than base_charge:
        set credit_used to base_charge
    let weekend_fee be 0
    if weekend_event:
        set weekend_fee to (full_price_guests plus concession_guests) times 175
    let due be base_charge minus credit_used plus weekend_fee
    give back due

to project_status giving service_status:

to handle_request with request as event_request giving event_response:

    let concession be request's concession_guests times 950
    let weekend_fee be 0

        set weekend_fee to (request's full_price_guests plus request's concession_guests) times 175
    let gross be full_price plus concession plus weekend_fee

    give back an event_response with full_price_charge_cents full_price, concession_charge_cents concession, weekend_fee_cents weekend_fee, gross_charge_cents gross, credit_used_cents credit_used, amount_due_cents due, payment_state state

The browser export returns power_score.

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Festival Power","ready":true}`.

- `light_rigs`: number

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub speaker_towers:i64,pub watts_each:i64,pub light_rigs:i64,pub weather_cover:bool} impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.speaker_towers>=0&&self.watts_each>=0&&self.light_rigs>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub speaker_watts:i64,pub lighting_watts:i64,pub weather_watts:i64,pub total_watts:i64,pub connection_points:i64,pub power_score:i64,pub power_mode:String}
pub fn festival_power_score(s:i64,w:i64,l:i64,c:bool)->i64{0}
pub fn handle(v:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let speaker=v.speaker_towers*v.watts_each;let lighting=v.light_rigs*900;let weather=if v.weather_cover{(v.speaker_towers+v.light_rigs)*75}else{0};let points=v.speaker_towers*3+v.light_rigs*5;ResponseOutput{speaker_watts:speaker,lighting_watts:lighting,weather_watts:weather,total_watts:speaker+lighting+weather,connection_points:points,power_score:festival_power_score(v.speaker_towers,v.watts_each,v.light_rigs,v.weather_cover),power_mode:if v.speaker_towers>0&&v.light_rigs>0{"mixed"}else if v.light_rigs>0{"lighting"}else{"audio"}.into()}}
#[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn parley_festival_power_score(a:i64,b:i64,c:i64,d:i32)->i64{festival_power_score(a,b,c,d!=0)}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_039::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { festival_power_score: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_festival_power_score(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Festival Power", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }

# Build a festival power planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Festival Power contract in the supplied stack. speaker_watts is speaker_towers * watts_each. lighting_watts is light_rigs * 900. weather_watts is (speaker_towers + light_rigs) * 75 when weather_cover is true and zero otherwise. total_watts is the sum of speaker, lighting, and weather watts. connection_points is speaker_towers * 3 + light_rigs * 5. power_score is total_watts + connection_points * 20. power_mode is mixed when both speakers and lights are present, lighting when only lights are present, and audio otherwise. The browser export returns power_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Festival Power","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/festival-power` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `speaker_towers`: number
- `watts_each`: number
- `light_rigs`: number
- `weather_cover`: yesno

Response fields:

- `speaker_watts`: number
- `lighting_watts`: number
- `weather_watts`: number
- `total_watts`: number
- `connection_points`: number
- `power_score`: number
- `power_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `festival_power_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`power_score` for equivalent inputs.

# Repair chilled-capacity propagation in seedling dispatch

Repair the supplied Seedling Dispatch application. shippable_trays is max(tray_count - reserved_trays, 0). base_capacity is van_count * 24. chill_buffer is van_count * 3 during chilled_transport and zero otherwise. dispatch_capacity is max(base_capacity - chill_buffer, 0). overflow_trays is max(shippable_trays - dispatch_capacity, 0). loaded_trays is min(shippable_trays, dispatch_capacity). space_remaining is max(dispatch_capacity - loaded_trays, 0). dispatch_state is overflow when overflow_trays is positive, loaded when loaded_trays is positive, and idle otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns overflow_trays.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Seedling Dispatch","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/seedling-dispatch` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `tray_count`: number
- `reserved_trays`: number
- `van_count`: number
- `chilled_transport`: yesno

Response fields:

- `shippable_trays`: number
- `base_capacity`: number
- `chill_buffer`: number
- `dispatch_capacity`: number
- `overflow_trays`: number
- `loaded_trays`: number
- `space_remaining`: number
- `dispatch_state`: text

## Browser

Export `seedling_overflow` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`overflow_trays` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/health/ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Seedling Dispatch", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v3/seedling-dispatch")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    tray_count: int = Field(ge=0); reserved_trays: int = Field(ge=0); van_count: int = Field(ge=0); chilled_transport: bool
def dispatch_capacity(vans: int, chilled: bool) -> int: return vans*24
def handle(v: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    ship=max(v.tray_count-v.reserved_trays,0); base=v.van_count*24; buffer=v.van_count*3 if v.chilled_transport else 0; cap=dispatch_capacity(v.van_count,v.chilled_transport); overflow=max(ship-cap,0); loaded=min(ship,cap)
    return {"shippable_trays":ship,"base_capacity":base,"chill_buffer":buffer,"dispatch_capacity":cap,"overflow_trays":overflow,"loaded_trays":loaded,"space_remaining":max(cap-loaded,0),"dispatch_state":"overflow" if overflow else "loaded" if loaded else "idle"}

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a festival power planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Festival Power contract in the supplied stack. speaker_watts is speaker_towers * watts_each. lighting_watts is light_rigs * 900. weather_watts is (speaker_towers + light_rigs) * 75 when weather_cover is true and zero otherwise. total_watts is the sum of speaker, lighting, and weather watts. connection_points is speaker_towers * 3 + light_rigs * 5. power_score is total_watts + connection_points * 20. power_mode is mixed when both speakers and lights are present, lighting when only lights are present, and audio otherwise. The browser export returns power_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Festival Power","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/festival-power` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `speaker_towers`: number
- `watts_each`: number
- `light_rigs`: number
- `weather_cover`: yesno

Response fields:

- `speaker_watts`: number
- `lighting_watts`: number
- `weather_watts`: number
- `total_watts`: number
- `connection_points`: number
- `power_score`: number
- `power_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `festival_power_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`power_score` for equivalent inputs.

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_039::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { festival_power_score: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_festival_power_score(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Festival Power", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_039_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/ready", get(status)).route("/api/v3/festival-power", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Build a festival power planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Festival Power contract in the supplied stack. speaker_watts is speaker_towers * watts_each. lighting_watts is light_rigs * 900. weather_watts is (speaker_towers + light_rigs) * 75 when weather_cover is true and zero otherwise. total_watts is the sum of speaker, lighting, and weather watts. connection_points is speaker_towers * 3 + light_rigs * 5. power_score is total_watts + connection_points * 20. power_mode is mixed when both speakers and lights are present, lighting when only lights are present, and audio otherwise. The browser export returns power_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Festival Power","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/festival-power` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `speaker_towers`: number
- `watts_each`: number
- `light_rigs`: number
- `weather_cover`: yesno

Response fields:

- `speaker_watts`: number
- `lighting_watts`: number
- `weather_watts`: number
- `total_watts`: number
- `connection_points`: number
- `power_score`: number
- `power_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `festival_power_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`power_score` for equivalent inputs.

#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub speaker_towers:i64,pub watts_each:i64,pub light_rigs:i64,pub weather_cover:bool} impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.speaker_towers>=0&&self.watts_each>=0&&self.light_rigs>=0}}
#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct ResponseOutput{pub speaker_watts:i64,pub lighting_watts:i64,pub weather_watts:i64,pub total_watts:i64,pub connection_points:i64,pub power_score:i64,pub power_mode:String}
pub fn festival_power_score(s:i64,w:i64,l:i64,c:bool)->i64{0}
pub fn handle(v:RequestInput)->ResponseOutput{let speaker=v.speaker_towers*v.watts_each;let lighting=v.light_rigs*900;let weather=if v.weather_cover{(v.speaker_towers+v.light_rigs)*75}else{0};let points=v.speaker_towers*3+v.light_rigs*5;ResponseOutput{speaker_watts:speaker,lighting_watts:lighting,weather_watts:weather,total_watts:speaker+lighting+weather,connection_points:points,power_score:festival_power_score(v.speaker_towers,v.watts_each,v.light_rigs,v.weather_cover),power_mode:if v.speaker_towers>0&&v.light_rigs>0{"mixed"}else if v.light_rigs>0{"lighting"}else{"audio"}.into()}}

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_039::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { festival_power_score: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_festival_power_score(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Festival Power", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_039_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/health/ready", get(status)).route("/api/v3/festival-power", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_039.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Repair prepaid event credit after weekend fees

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Event Credit","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/event-credit` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a festival power planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Festival Power contract in the supplied stack. speaker_watts is speaker_towers * watts_each. lighting_watts is light_rigs * 900. weather_watts is (speaker_towers + light_rigs) * 75 when weather_cover is true and zero otherwise. total_watts is the sum of speaker, lighting, and weather watts. connection_points is speaker_towers * 3 + light_rigs * 5. power_score is total_watts + connection_points * 20. power_mode is mixed when both speakers and lights are present, lighting when only lights are present, and audio otherwise. The browser export returns power_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Festival Power","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/festival-power` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `speaker_towers`: number
- `watts_each`: number
- `light_rigs`: number
- `weather_cover`: yesno

Response fields:

- `speaker_watts`: number
- `lighting_watts`: number
- `weather_watts`: number
- `total_watts`: number
- `connection_points`: number
- `power_score`: number
- `power_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `festival_power_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`power_score` for equivalent inputs.

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a festival power planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Festival Power contract in the supplied stack. speaker_watts is speaker_towers * watts_each. lighting_watts is light_rigs * 900. weather_watts is (speaker_towers + light_rigs) * 75 when weather_cover is true and zero otherwise. total_watts is the sum of speaker, lighting, and weather watts. connection_points is speaker_towers * 3 + light_rigs * 5. power_score is total_watts + connection_points * 20. power_mode is mixed when both speakers and lights are present, lighting when only lights are present, and audio otherwise. The browser export returns power_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Festival Power","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/festival-power` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `speaker_towers`: number
- `watts_each`: number
- `light_rigs`: number
- `weather_cover`: yesno

Response fields:

- `speaker_watts`: number
- `lighting_watts`: number
- `weather_watts`: number
- `total_watts`: number
- `connection_points`: number
- `power_score`: number
- `power_mode`: text

## Browser

Export `festival_power_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`power_score` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/health/ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Festival Power", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v3/festival-power")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
class RequestInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True)
    speaker_towers: int = Field(ge=0); watts_each: int = Field(ge=0); light_rigs: int = Field(ge=0); weather_cover: bool
def festival_power_score(s: int, w: int, l: int, cover: bool) -> int: return 0
def handle(v: RequestInput) -> dict[str, object]:
    speaker=v.speaker_towers*v.watts_each; lighting=v.light_rigs*900; weather=(v.speaker_towers+v.light_rigs)*75 if v.weather_cover else 0; points=v.speaker_towers*3+v.light_rigs*5
    return {"speaker_watts":speaker,"lighting_watts":lighting,"weather_watts":weather,"total_watts":speaker+lighting+weather,"connection_points":points,"power_score":festival_power_score(v.speaker_towers,v.watts_each,v.light_rigs,v.weather_cover),"power_mode":"mixed" if v.speaker_towers and v.light_rigs else "lighting" if v.light_rigs else "audio"}

# Repair prepaid event credit after weekend fees

Repair the supplied Event Credit application. full_price_charge_cents is full_price_guests * 1800. concession_charge_cents is concession_guests * 950. weekend_fee_cents is (full_price_guests + concession_guests) * 175 during a weekend_event and zero otherwise. gross_charge_cents is the sum of full-price, concession, and weekend charges. credit_used_cents is min(prepaid_credit_cents, gross_charge_cents). amount_due_cents is max(gross_charge_cents - prepaid_credit_cents, 0). payment_state is covered when amount_due_cents is zero and due otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns amount_due_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Event Credit","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/event-credit` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `full_price_guests`: number
- `concession_guests`: number
- `prepaid_credit_cents`: number
- `weekend_event`: yesno

Response fields:

- `full_price_charge_cents`: number
- `concession_charge_cents`: number
- `weekend_fee_cents`: number
- `gross_charge_cents`: number
- `credit_used_cents`: number
- `amount_due_cents`: number
- `payment_state`: text

## Browser

Export `event_amount_due` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`amount_due_cents` for equivalent inputs.

use serde::{Deserialize,Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] pub struct RequestInput{pub full_price_guests:i64,pub concession_guests:i64,pub prepaid_credit_cents:i64,pub weekend_event:bool} impl RequestInput{pub fn valid(&self)->bool{self.full_price_guests>=0&&self.concession_guests>=0&&self.prepaid_credit_cents>=0}}

# Repair prepaid event credit after weekend fees

Repair the supplied Event Credit application. full_price_charge_cents is full_price_guests * 1800. concession_charge_cents is concession_guests * 950. weekend_fee_cents is (full_price_guests + concession_guests) * 175 during a weekend_event and zero otherwise. gross_charge_cents is the sum of full-price, concession, and weekend charges. credit_used_cents is min(prepaid_credit_cents, gross_charge_cents). amount_due_cents is max(gross_charge_cents - prepaid_credit_cents, 0). payment_state is covered when amount_due_cents is zero and due otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns amount_due_cents.

## HTTP

- `GET /health/ready` returns `{"service":"Event Credit","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v3/event-credit` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `full_price_guests`: number
- `concession_guests`: number
- `prepaid_credit_cents`: number
- `weekend_event`: yesno

Response fields:

- `full_price_charge_cents`: number
- `concession_charge_cents`: number
- `weekend_fee_cents`: number
- `gross_charge_cents`: number
- `credit_used_cents`: number
- `amount_due_cents`: number
- `payment_state`: text

## Browser

Export `event_amount_due` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`amount_due_cents` for equivalent inputs.
